habitat: Singly or in pairs in dense riparian vegetation, reed beds and thickets away from water.
summary: A common resident. Rufous wings, a black cap and tail, and white underparts, with unbarred upper tail coverts. The tail is shorter than that of a Coppery-tailed Coucal and has green iridescence, and the bill is less heavy. The immature is duller, with black barring above and finely buff-barred upper tail coverts. Newman’s page does not describe the voice. The stub has no Kemp estimate and none was added.

similar.note: Burchell’s Coucal has finely barred upper tail coverts. Senegal Coucal has those coverts unbarred. Newman says the ranges are mutually exclusive.

population.notes: No sourced Kruger estimate is currently available; taxonomy or later records require separate research.

bill.shape: Less heavy than a Coppery-tailed Coucal.

tail.shape: Shorter than a Coppery-tailed Coucal, with green iridescence.

upperparts.pattern: Duller. Upper parts barred black and upper tail coverts finely barred buff.

viewNotes.note: Black cap, rufous wing and white underparts. The upper tail coverts are unbarred.
White underparts and a black cap.
Black tail with green iridescence, and unbarred upper tail coverts.
The upperwing was named only as rufous.
White underparts. The underside of the wing was not named.

calls.description: Newman’s species page does not describe the voice. Grade A call from Cairo. The filename is the generic coucal.mp3. The only South African file found was a grade D Kruger recording, so the higher grade was kept.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Newman calls it a common resident. Length is from Newman’s Birds. The stub has no Kemp block and no estimate, and both were left that way. Newman says the range does not overlap Burchell’s Coucal, but both species are on the Kruger list.
